newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia denies ASEAN seeking help on Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia denies ASEAN seeking help on Cambodia.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Friday that the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) had not sought the help of Indonesia and France to defuse the political crisis in Cambodia.
Alatas said the crisis was an internal affair for Cambodia and it was not possible for France or Indonesia to interfere, the official Antara news agency reported.
"It is impossible for Indonesia and France to step in as Cambodia is a sovereign country," he was quoted as saying. "We must respect this sovereignty."

A Thai foreign ministry official said on Thursday that ASEAN ministers who were in Hong Kong earlier in the week for the territory's handover to China decided at an informal meeting to request Jakarta and Paris for help in the Cambodian crisis.

Political tension has been high in Cambodia over a long-running power struggle between the country's two prime ministers who head a deadlocked coalition government. Their feud has been inflamed in recent weeks with the unravelling of the Khmer Rouge guerrilla force.
France and Indonesia both played major roles in pushing Cambodia's warring factions towards the 1991 Paris peace accord that officially ended the country's civil war.

Alatas said the ministers did discuss Cambodia while they were in Hong Kong but added that the only decision taken was that ASEAN would offer technical assistance on preparations for general elections to be held there next year.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Burma, Cambodia and Laos are to join later this year.
